name: Learn: Assemble a Hardened Deployment
objective: Capstone practical: assemble ONE Deployment that satisfies ~10 interlocking production requirements — config + secret injection, emptyDir, full securityContext hardening, exact resources, a probe, a dedicated SA, and its Service. Graded strictly, per requirement, with the exact reason for anything you miss. This is the 'put it all together' skill the exam tests and most practice skips.
description: A single composite object with 10 exactly-graded requirements. Build it from the brief; the Check panel shows which requirements you nailed and which you missed, with reasons.

questions.title: Build the hardened 'checkout' Deployment + Service (read the whole brief first)
questions.teach:
This is a capstone: one Deployment + Service that must satisfy ~10 interlocking requirements at once — identity, config, storage, security, resources, health, exposure. The skill is assembling it from a dense brief without missing a field. Scaffold with `kubectl create deployment … --dry-run=client -o yaml`, then hand-edit the hard parts.

**Gotcha:** every value is graded **exactly** — a missing `tier=api` label, UID `1000` instead of `1001`, `cpu: 200m` instead of `100m`, or `targetPort: 8080` instead of `80` each loses marks. Check field-by-field against the brief before you submit.
questions.prompt:
The payments team needs their **checkout API** deployed to the **`shop`** namespace. The namespace already contains a ConfigMap `checkout-cfg`, a Secret `checkout-sec`, and a ServiceAccount `checkout-sa` — **wire them in; do not recreate them**.

Create a Deployment **`checkout`** meeting ALL of the following, then expose it. Every bullet is graded exactly.

- **3** replicas; image **`nginx:1.27-alpine`**; container named **`api`** (exactly one container).
- Pod template labelled **`app=checkout`** AND **`tier=api`**; selector matches `app=checkout`.
- Run under ServiceAccount **`checkout-sa`** (not `default`).
- **Bulk-inject** every key of ConfigMap `checkout-cfg` as env; **and** set env **`API_KEY`** from the `API_KEY` key of Secret `checkout-sec`.
- Mount an **`emptyDir`** at **`/var/cache/checkout`**.
- Container security: **read-only root filesystem**, run as **non-root** with **UID 1001**, **drop ALL** capabilities.
- Resources: requests **cpu=100m, memory=128Mi**; limits **cpu=250m, memory=256Mi**.
- Readiness probe: **HTTP GET `/` on port 80**, `initialDelaySeconds=5`, `periodSeconds=10`.
- Expose with a **ClusterIP** Service **`checkout`** on port **8080** → container port **80**.

All in namespace `shop`. (Grading checks the object spec, not whether the read-only pod starts.)
questions.hint: Scaffold, then harden: `kubectl -n shop create deployment checkout --image=nginx:1.27-alpine --replicas=3 --dry-run=client -o yaml > d.yaml`, then edit in: the container name `api`, `serviceAccountName`, `envFrom`+`env`, the `emptyDir` volume+mount, `securityContext` (readOnlyRootFilesystem/runAsNonRoot/runAsUser 1001/capabilities drop ALL), `resources`, `readinessProbe`, and the `tier=api` label. Then `kubectl -n shop expose deployment checkout --name checkout --port 8080 --target-port 80` (verify it's ClusterIP). Check your work field-by-field against the brief before you Check.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: checkout, namespace: shop }
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: checkout } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: checkout, tier: api } }
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: checkout-sa
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        envFrom: [ { configMapRef: { name: checkout-cfg } } ]
        env:
        - name: API_KEY
          valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: checkout-sec, key: API_KEY } }
        volumeMounts: [ { name: cache, mountPath: /var/cache/checkout } ]
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1001
          capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }
          limits: { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: { path: /, port: 80 }
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes: [ { name: cache, emptyDir: {} } ]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: checkout, namespace: shop }
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector: { app: checkout }
  ports: [ { port: 8080, targetPort: 80 } ]
YAML

verification.description: Deployment checkout: 3 replicas, one container 'api' on image nginx:1.27-alpine
Pod labels app=checkout + tier=api; selector app=checkout
env API_KEY from Secret checkout-sec key API_KEY
securityContext: readOnlyRootFilesystem, runAsNonRoot, UID 1001, drop ALL caps
Service checkout: ClusterIP 8080 -> targetPort 80, selector app=checkout

questions.eli5:
This is the final boss: instead of one small skill, you build **one Deployment that does everything at once** — like assembling a whole flat-pack wardrobe from a long instruction sheet where every single screw is graded. Miss one screw and you lose a point, even if the wardrobe stands.

The scenario: the payments team wants their **checkout API** running in the `shop` room. Three identical workers (replicas), running the nginx image, in a container that must be named exactly `api`. The room already has a config board (ConfigMap), a locked box (Secret), and an ID badge (ServiceAccount) prepared — your job is to **wire them in, not remake them**.

Then you pile on all the good habits from earlier lessons at once: bulk-inject the config board as env vars; pull one secret into `API_KEY`; give it a scratch drawer (`emptyDir`); harden it (read-only root, non-root UID 1001, drop all special powers); set exact CPU/memory requests and limits; add a readiness check; and finally put a front door on it (a ClusterIP Service on port 8080 forwarding to the container's port 80).

The smart move: don't hand-type the whole thing. Scaffold with `kubectl create deployment ... --dry-run=client -o yaml`, then edit in the hard parts. Then check **field by field** against the brief before submitting.

**Watch out for:**

- **Every value is graded EXACTLY.** UID `1001` not `1000`; cpu `100m` not `200m`; `targetPort 80` not `8080`; the `tier=api` label must be present. One wrong number = lost mark.
- **Two labels on the pod template** (`app=checkout` AND `tier=api`), but the **selector matches only `app=checkout`**.
- **Wire in the existing SA/ConfigMap/Secret by name** — do not recreate them.
- **Service `port` (8080) ≠ `targetPort` (80)** — the Service listens on 8080 and forwards to the container's 80.
- **It's `envFrom` for the bulk ConfigMap AND a separate `env` entry** for the single `API_KEY` secret — two different mechanisms, both required.
- **The read-only pod may not actually start** — grading checks the spec, not a running pod, so don't panic if it crashloops.
questions.deepDive:
## Capstone: a hardened Deployment + Service

### Mental model
One object that composes **every** config/security/health skill at once: identity (ServiceAccount), config (ConfigMap `envFrom` + Secret `env`), storage (`emptyDir`), hardening (`securityContext`), exact `resources`, a `readinessProbe`, and exposure (ClusterIP Service). The skill is translating a dense brief into fields **without missing one** — each is graded exactly. Scaffold imperatively, then hand-edit.

### Scaffold, then harden
```bash
kubectl -n shop create deployment checkout \
  --image=nginx:1.27-alpine --replicas=3 --dry-run=client -o yaml > d.yaml
# edit in: container name 'api', serviceAccountName, envFrom+env, emptyDir volume+mount,
#          securityContext, resources, readinessProbe, and the tier=api label
kubectl apply -f d.yaml
kubectl -n shop expose deployment checkout --name checkout --port 8080 --target-port 80
```

### The full manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: checkout, namespace: shop }
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: checkout } }        # selector: app=checkout only
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: checkout, tier: api } } # BOTH labels on the pod
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: checkout-sa                  # existing SA — don't recreate
      containers:
      - name: api                                      # exact container name
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        envFrom: [ { configMapRef: { name: checkout-cfg } } ]   # bulk config
        env:
        - name: API_KEY
          valueFrom: { secretKeyRef: { name: checkout-sec, key: API_KEY } }
        volumeMounts: [ { name: cache, mountPath: /var/cache/checkout } ]
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1001                              # exact UID
          capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
        resources:
          requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }       # exact
          limits:   { cpu: 250m, memory: 256Mi }       # exact
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: { path: /, port: 80 }
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
      volumes: [ { name: cache, emptyDir: {} } ]
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: { name: checkout, namespace: shop }
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector: { app: checkout }
  ports: [ { port: 8080, targetPort: 80 } ]            # 8080 → container 80
```

### Requirement → field map (graded exactly)
| Requirement | Field |
|---|---|
| 3 replicas, image, one container `api` | `spec.replicas`, `containers[0].name/image` |
| labels app+tier, selector app | `template.metadata.labels`, `spec.selector.matchLabels` |
| run as `checkout-sa` | `template.spec.serviceAccountName` |
| bulk ConfigMap env | `envFrom.configMapRef` |
| `API_KEY` from Secret | `env.valueFrom.secretKeyRef` |
| emptyDir at path | `volumes[].emptyDir` + `volumeMounts` |
| RO root, non-root UID 1001, drop ALL | container `securityContext` |
| requests/limits exact | `resources` |
| readiness HTTP / :80 | `readinessProbe.httpGet` |
| ClusterIP 8080→80 | Service `type`/`ports` |

### Service port vs targetPort
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `port` | port the Service listens on (**8080**) |
| `targetPort` | container port traffic is sent to (**80**) |
| `type: ClusterIP` | internal-only virtual IP (default) |

### Verify field-by-field
```bash
kubectl -n shop get deploy checkout -o yaml | less
kubectl -n shop get deploy checkout -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName}'; echo
kubectl -n shop get deploy checkout -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.metadata.labels}'; echo
kubectl -n shop get svc checkout -o jsonpath='{.spec.type} {.spec.ports[0].port}->{.spec.ports[0].targetPort}'; echo
kubectl -n shop rollout status deploy/checkout     # may not go Ready (RO root) — spec is what's graded
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Exact values**: UID 1001 (not 1000), cpu `100m`/`250m`, mem `128Mi`/`256Mi`, `targetPort 80`. One off = lost mark.
- **Two pod labels** (`app=checkout` + `tier=api`); **selector = app=checkout only** (selectors are immutable — don't add `tier`).
- **Wire in existing SA/ConfigMap/Secret by name** — recreating them is wrong.
- **`envFrom` (bulk) AND `env` (single `API_KEY`)** are both required — different mechanisms.
- **Service `port` 8080 ≠ `targetPort` 80** — a classic swap mistake.
- **Container name must be `api`** — the scaffold defaults to the deployment name.
- **RO-root pod may crashloop** — grading inspects the **spec**, not a running pod; don't "fix" it by dropping the requirement.
- **`runAsNonRoot` + `runAsUser: 1001`** together satisfy non-root; omitting the UID leaves it image-dependent.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n shop create deployment checkout --image=nginx:1.27-alpine --replicas=3 --dry-run=client -o yaml > d.yaml
# hand-edit all fields per the brief, then:
kubectl apply -f d.yaml
kubectl -n shop expose deployment checkout --name checkout --port 8080 --target-port 80
```
